title: Judgement in the Age of Jev: From Evaluation Scarcity to Evaluation Abundance
abstract: arXiv:2610.01231v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has reduced the cost of producing plausible symbolic artefacts, leading recent organisation scholarship to identify evaluation and discernment as constraints under conditions of production abundance. This perspective examines a further possibility: that machine evaluation itself becomes inexpensive enough to be deployed routinely and at scale. The investigation is prompted by Jev, TypeSafe AI's specialised model for typed probabilistic decisions. TypeSafe explicitly invokes William Stanley Jevons to argue that lower-cost machine intelligence can unlock previously uneconomic uses. translated_title: Jev时代的判断：从评估稀缺到评估丰裕
translated_abstract: 生成式人工智能降低了生产看似合理的符号化成果的成本，近期组织学术研究因此将评估与鉴别能力视为生产丰裕条件下的制约因素。本文展望进一步的可能性：机器评估本身变得足够廉价，从而能够被常规化、规模化地部署。这项研究源于Jev——TypeSafe AI公司用于类型化概率决策的专用模型。TypeSafe明确援引威廉·斯坦利·杰文斯，主张更低成本的机器智能可以解锁此前不具经济性的应用场景。本文将其视为一种技术性启发而非已确立的实证结果，提出了针对机器评估的条件性杰文斯假说：在潜在需求充足的情况下，可用机器评估的总边际成本若出现足够大幅的下降，可能会提升其组织层面的使用量。
tldr: 本文提出“条件性杰文斯假说”，认为机器评估成本的大幅下降在潜在需求充足时会显著提升组织对机器评估的使用量，使判断从评估稀缺走向评估丰裕。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a conditional Jevons hypothesis: sufficiently large reductions in the marginal cost of machine evaluation may substantially increase its organisational consumption, shifting judgement from evaluation scarcity to evaluation abundance.
